UNH.rationale: UNH presents a mixed but moderately attractive picture. On fundamentals, the company is a massive, diversified healthcare franchise with $112B quarterly revenues, strong gross margins (~88%), and robust cash generation ($8.9B operating cash flow in Q1 2026, $11.1B in Q2). The Q2 2026 earnings report (July 16) was a significant positive surprise: adjusted EPS of $6.38 beat consensus of ~$4.90 by 31.6%, the medical care ratio improved to 86.7% from 89.4% YoY, and management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $19.50-$20.00 from $18.25+. Operating earnings surged 55% YoY to $8.0B. However, the growth trajectory is mixed — revenue grew only 2% YoY, membership is declining (Medicare Advantage down 965K since year-end 2025, total UnitedHealthcare down 525K sequentially), and the company is deliberately shrinking its footprint to protect margins. Net margin has compressed from ~5.6% to ~2.8% over the past year, and ROE has fallen from ~22% to ~12%. The balance sheet is solid with $104B equity and manageable leverage (41.2% debt-to-capital). On valuation, the stock trades at 30x diluted PE — near the top of its 365-day range (9.5-30.7) and well above the ~14x level from early 2026. P/B of 3.71 is also at the top of its range (2.2-3.8). This is expensive relative to recent history, though the raised guidance implies ~21-22x forward adjusted earnings, which is more reasonable. The near-term catalyst is the massive Q2 earnings beat and guidance raise, which drove a 7%+ stock move and should support analyst estimate revisions upward. However, significant risks remain: DOJ antitrust investigation into Medicare billing practices, claims denial lawsuits, membership contraction, and the question of whether margin recovery is sustainable or a value trap. Berkshire Hathaway's full exit from UNH is a negative signal. The stock has rallied 35% in the past quarter, which may have already priced in much of the good news. Net: solid franchise with improving near-term earnings trajectory, but expensive vs history, membership headwinds, and regulatory overhangs temper enthusiasm.
